0.en: b. The observation of self-consciousness in its purity and in its relation to external actuality; logical and psychological laws
0.zh: b. 对自我意识在其纯粹性中以及在其与外部现实性的关系中的观察；逻辑规律和心理学规律

en: The observation of nature finds the concept realized in inorganic nature, namely laws whose moments are things that at the same time comport themselves as abstractions; but this concept is not a simplicity reflected into itself, the life of organic nature is on the other hand only this simplicity reflected into itself; the opposition of itself, as that of the universal and the individual, does not fall apart within the essence of this life itself; the essence is not the genus, which in its undifferentiated element would divide and move itself and in its opposition would at the same time be undifferentiated for itself.
Observation finds this free concept, whose universality has developed individuality just as absolutely within itself, only in the concept itself that exists as concept, or in self-consciousness.
zh: 对自然的观察发现概念在无机自然中得到了实现，也就是那些规律，它们的各个环节是物，而这些物同时又作为抽象物在活动；但这个概念并不是一种在自身中反思过的单一性，有机自然的生命则只是这种在自身中反思过的单一性；它自身作为普遍物与个别物的对立，并没有在这种生命本身的本质中分离开来；这个本质并不是类，即那个在其无差别的元素中会分裂并运动、并在其对立中同时自为地是无差别的类。
观察发现，这个自由的概念，也就是其普遍性同样绝对地在自身中拥有展开的个别性的概念，只存在于那个作为概念而存在着的概念本身中，或者只存在于自我意识中。

en: Now, in that it turns into itself and directs itself upon the concept that is actual as free concept, it first finds the laws of thought.
This individuality, which thinking is on its own account, is the abstract movement of the negative wholly taken back into simplicity, and the laws are outside reality.
– That they have no reality means, quite generally, nothing other than: they are without truth.
They are indeed supposed to be not whole truth, but still formal truth.
But the purely formal without reality is the thought-thing, or the empty abstraction without the division in it, which would be nothing other than the content.

But on the other side, since they are laws of pure thinking, while this is the universal in itself and hence a knowing that immediately has being, and therein all reality, on it, these laws are absolute concepts and inseparably the essentialities of form as of things.
Since the universality that moves within itself is the self-divided simple concept, it thereby has content in itself, and a content that is all content, only not a sensuous being.

It is a content that is neither in contradiction with the form nor at all separated from it, but is rather essentially the form itself; for this is nothing other than the universal that divides itself into its pure moments.
zh: 当它现在转向自身之内，并指向那个作为自由概念而现实的概念时，它首先找到的是思维的规律。
这种个别性，即思维在它自身上所是的个别性，就是那种抽象的、完全被收回到单一性之中的否定物的运动，而这些规律则在实在性之外。
——它们没有实在性，一般说来无非意味着：它们没有真理。
它们虽然也不应当是完整的真理，但毕竟应当是形式的真理。
但纯粹形式的东西若没有实在性，就是思想物，或者说就是那种在自身上没有分裂的空洞抽象，而这种分裂无非就是内容。
但在另一方面，由于它们是纯粹思维的规律，而纯粹思维又是自在地普遍的东西，因而是一种知识，这种知识直接在自身上拥有存在、并在其中拥有一切实在性，所以这些规律是绝对的概念，并且不可分离地是形式和物的本质。
由于在自身中运动着的普遍性是那自身分裂了的简单概念，所以它以这种方式在自身上拥有内容，而且是一种这样的内容：它是一切内容，只是不是感性的存在。
这是一种内容，它既不与形式相矛盾，也根本不与形式分离，而毋宁说本质上就是形式本身；因为形式无非就是那个把自己分裂成它那些纯粹环节的普遍物。

en: But as this form or content is for observation as observation, it receives the determination of a found, given, that is, merely existing content.

It becomes the calm being of relations, a multitude of separated necessities, which as a firm content are supposed to have truth in and for themselves, in their determinacy, and are thus in fact withdrawn from the form.
– But this absolute truth of fixed determinacies, or of many different laws, contradicts the unity of self-consciousness, or of thinking and of form in general.
Whatever is asserted as a firm law that persists in itself can only be a moment of the unity reflecting itself into itself, and can appear only as a vanishing magnitude.
But torn out of this context of movement by observation and placed singly, they do not lack content, for they have a determinate content, but rather they lack the form, which is their essence.

In fact it is not because they are supposed to be merely formal and to have no content, but rather for the opposite reason, because in their determinacy, or precisely as a content from which the form has been taken, they are supposed to count as something absolute, that these laws are not the truth of thinking.
In their truth, as moments vanishing in the unity of thinking, they would have to be taken as knowing, or as thinking movement, but not as laws of knowing.
But observing is not knowing itself and does not know it, but rather inverts its nature into the shape of being, that is, it grasps its negativity only as laws of being.
– Here it is sufficient to have shown the invalidity of the so-called laws of thought from the general nature of the matter.

The closer development belongs in speculative philosophy, in which they show themselves as what they are in truth, namely individual vanishing moments, whose truth is only the whole of the thinking movement, knowing itself.
zh: 但就这种形式或内容对于作为观察的观察而言所是的样子来说，它获得的是被找到的、被给予的、也就是说仅仅存在着的内容的规定。
它变成了种种关系的静止的存在，一大堆被分离出来的必然性，这些必然性作为固定的内容应当自在自为地、在其规定性中拥有真理，因此实际上被抽离了形式。
——但这种固定规定性的、或许多不同规律的绝对真理，却与自我意识的统一，或者说与思维以及一般意义上的形式的统一相矛盾。
凡被说成是固定的、自在地持存的规律的东西，都只能是那种在自身中反思自身的统一的一个环节，只能作为一种消逝着的量出现。
但如果被考察从这种运动的联系中抽出来、被单独地摆在那里，它们缺的就不是内容，因为它们有一种特定的内容，而是毋宁说缺少形式，而形式才是它们的本质。
实际上，这些规律之所以不是思维的真理，并不是因为它们应当只是形式的、不应当有内容，而是毋宁说出自相反的理由，因为它们在它们的规定性中、或者说恰恰作为被拿掉了形式的内容，应当被视为某种绝对的东西。
在它们的真理中，即作为在思维的统一中消逝着的环节，它们就必须被当作知识或思维的运动，而不是被当作知识的规律。
但观察并不是知识本身，也不认识知识，而是把知识的本性颠倒成存在的形态，也就是说，只把它的否定性把握为存在的规律。
——在这里，从事情的一般本性出发指明所谓思维规律的无效性，就已经足够了。
更切近的展开属于思辨哲学，在那里它们会显示出它们真正所是的东西，即一些个别的、消逝着的环节，而这些环节的真理只是思维运动的整体，即知识本身。

en: This negative unity of thinking is for itself, or rather it is being-for-itself, the principle of individuality, and in its reality doing consciousness.
To it, as the reality of those laws, observing consciousness is therefore led on by the nature of the matter.

Since this connection is not for it, it supposes that thinking with its laws remains standing for it on the one side, and that on the other side it obtains another being in what is now its object, namely doing consciousness, which is for itself in such a way that it sublates otherness and in this intuition of itself as the negative has its actuality.
zh: 思维的这个否定性的统一是自为的，或者毋宁说，它就是自为存在，是个体性的原则，并且在它的实在性中就是行动着的意识。
因此，观察的意识被事情的本性继续引向它，即引向那些规律的实在性。
由于这种联系不是为它的，它就以为，思维连同它的规律在它这一边停住不动，而在另一边它则在那个现在成为它对象的东西上获得另一种存在，即行动着的意识，这种意识如此自为地存在，以致它扬弃了他在，并且在这种把自己当作否定物的直观中拥有自己的现实性。

en: Thus a new field opens up for observation in the acting actuality of consciousness.

Psychology contains the multitude of laws according to which spirit comports itself differently toward the various modes of its actuality, as toward a found otherness; partly to receive these into itself and to become conformable to the found habits, customs and way of thinking, as that in which it is an object to itself as actuality, partly to know itself as self-active against them, to pick out for itself, with inclination and passion, only something particular from them, and to make the objective conformable to itself, – there to comport itself negatively toward itself as individuality, here toward itself as universal being.

– Independence, on the first side, gives to the found material only the form of conscious individuality in general and, as regards the content, remains standing within the found universal actuality; but on the other side it gives it at least a peculiar modification that does not contradict its essential content, or also one through which the individual, as particular actuality and peculiar content, opposes itself to it – and becomes crime, in that it sublates it in a merely individual way, or in that it does this in a universal way and thereby for all, and brings another world, another right, law and customs in the place of the existing ones.
zh: 于是，在意识的行动着的现实性那里，为观察打开了一片新的领域。

心理学包含着大量规律，精神依照这些规律而对它的现实性的各种方式，即作为一种被找到的他在，采取不同的态度；它一方面要把这些方式接纳到自身中，并变得符合那些被找到的习惯、风俗和思维方式，即在其中它作为现实性而对自己成为对象的东西，另一方面则要针对它们而知道自己是在自主活动的，带着爱好和激情只从中为自己挑出特殊的东西，并使那些对象性的东西符合自己，——在那里是对作为个别性的自己、在这里则是对作为普遍存在的自己采取否定的态度。

——独立性按照第一方面只给被找到的东西赋予一般意义上的有意识的个体性这一形式，并且在内容方面停留在被找到的普遍现实性之内；但按照另一方面，它至少给它一种独特的改变，这种改变并不与它的本质内容相矛盾，或者也给它这样一种改变：通过这种改变，个体作为特殊的现实性和独特的内容而与它对立起来——并且成为犯罪，因为它以一种仅仅个别的方式扬弃它，或者因为它以普遍的方式、从而为所有人这样做，把另一个世界、另一种法权、规律和风俗搬到现存的东西的位置上。

en: Observing psychology, which first expresses its perceptions of the universal ways that occur to it in acting consciousness, finds various faculties, inclinations and passions, and since the recollection of the unity of self-consciousness cannot be suppressed in the recounting of this collection, it must at least proceed to astonishment that in the spirit, as in a sack, so much and such heterogeneous, mutually contingent stuff can be together, especially since these show themselves not as dead, resting things but as restless movements.
zh: 观察的心理学首先说出它对于在行动的意识身上出现的那些普遍方式的知觉，它找到各种各样的能力、倾向和激情，而由于在讲述这一堆东西时，对自我意识之统一的回忆无法被压制下去，它至少必须一直走到惊奇：在精神里，就像在一个袋子里，竟能有如此多种多样的、如此不同类而彼此偶然的东西凑在一起，尤其是因为它们并不表现为死的、静止的东西，而是表现为不安的运动。

en: In the recounting of these various faculties, observation is on the universal side; the unity of these manifold capacities is the side opposed to this universality, actual individuality.

– But to grasp and recount the distinct actual individualities in such a way that the one human being has more inclination to this, the other more to that, the one more understanding than the other, has something far more uninteresting than even to enumerate the species of insects, mosses, etc.; for these give observation the right to take them thus singly and without concept, because they essentially belong to the element of contingent singling-out.
To take conscious individuality, by contrast, spiritlessly as a single existing appearance, has the contradictory character that its essence is the universal of spirit.
But in that apprehension at the same time lets it enter into the form of universality, it finds its law and now seems to have a rational purpose and to carry on a necessary business.
zh: 在讲述这些不同的能力时，观察处在普遍的那一面；这些多种多样能力的统一则是与这种普遍性相对立的那一面，即现实的个体性。
——但把这些有区别的、现实的个体性又这样来领会和讲述：这一个人更多地倾向于这种，另一个人更多地倾向于那种，这一个人比另一个人更有知性——这却比列举昆虫、苔藓等等的种还要无聊得多；因为后者给了观察以权利，把它们这样单个地、无概念地来看待，因为它们本质上属于偶然的个别化这一要素。
与此相反，把有意识的个体性无精神地当作单个存在着的现象来把握，却含有这样的矛盾：它的本质是精神的普遍之物。
但是，既然这种领会同时让它进入普遍性的形式，它就找到了自己的规律，现在似乎有了一个理性的目的，并且在从事一件必要的事情。

en: The moments that make up the content of the law are on the one hand individuality itself, on the other hand its universal inorganic nature, namely the circumstances, situation, habits, customs, religion etc. that are found at hand; out of these the determinate individuality is to be comprehended.
They contain the determinate as well as the universal and are at the same time something at hand that offers itself to observation and on the other side expresses itself in the form of individuality.
zh: 构成规律之内容的那些环节，一方面是个体性本身，另一方面是它的普遍的、无机的自然，即那些现成被发现的处境、状况、习惯、风俗、宗教等等；确定的个体性要从这些东西出发才能以概念把握。
它们既包含确定的东西，也包含普遍的东西，同时又是现成存在的东西，它呈现给观察，并且在另一面以个体性的形式表达出来。

en: The law of this relation of the two sides would now have to contain what effect and influence these determinate circumstances exercise on individuality.

But this individuality is precisely this: to be the universal as well, and therefore to flow together in a calm, immediate way with the universal that is at hand, with customs, habits etc., and to become conformable to them, as also to behave in opposition to them and rather to invert them – and likewise to behave quite indifferently toward them in its singleness, not to let them act upon it and not to be active against them.

What is to have influence on individuality, and what influence it is to have – which is really the same thing – therefore depends only on individuality itself; that this individuality has thereby become this determinate one means nothing else than: it has already been this.

Circumstances, situation, customs etc., which are shown on the one hand as at hand and on the other hand in this determinate individuality, express only the indeterminate essence of the latter, which is not what is at stake.

If these circumstances, way of thinking, customs, the condition of the world in general had not been, then the individual would indeed not have become what it is; for all who find themselves in this condition of the world are this universal substance.

– But as it has particularized itself in this individual – and such an individual is to be comprehended – so it would have had to particularize itself in and for itself and, in this determinacy that it has given itself, to have acted upon an individual; only thus would it have made it into this determinate one that it is.
If the outer were constituted in and for itself as it appears on individuality, then the latter would be comprehended out of the former.

We would have a doubled gallery of images, the one a reflection of the other; the one the gallery of the complete determinacy and delimitation of outer circumstances, the other the same translated into the manner in which they are in the conscious essence; the former the spherical surface, the latter the centre that represents it within itself.
zh: 这两方面之关系的规律，现在必须包含：这些确定的处境对个体性产生出什么样的作用和影响。
但是，这种个体性恰恰就是这样一回事：既是普遍之物，因而以平静而直接的方式与现成存在的普遍之物、即风俗、习惯等等交融在一起并变得合乎它们，又是与它们相对立地行动、宁可把它们颠倒过来——同样也是对它们采取在其个别性中完全漠不相关的态度，不让它们作用于自己，也不对它们有所行动。
什么东西应当对个体性有影响、又应当有怎样的影响——这其实是同一个意思——，因此只取决于个体性本身；说这种个体性由此变成了这个确定的个体性，无非是说：它早就已经是这样了。
处境、状况、风俗等等，一方面被表明为现成存在的，另一方面又被表明为存在于这个确定的个体性之中的，它们所表达的只是个体性那种不确定的本质，而事情并不在于这种本质。
如果这些处境、思维方式、风俗、总的世界状况不曾存在，那么个体当然就不会成为它所是的那个东西；因为处在这种世界状况中的一切人都是这种普遍实体。
——但是，它既然在这个个体身上——而这样的个体是应当被以概念把握的——把自己特殊化了，那么它就必须自在自为地把自己特殊化，并且以它赋予自己的这种规定性对一个个体发生作用；只有这样，它才会把这个个体造成它所是的这个确定的个体。
如果外在的东西自在自为地就是这样构成的，如同它在个体性身上显现出来的那样，那么这种个体性就会从那个外在的东西出发而被以概念把握。
我们就会有一个双重的图像长廊，其中一个是另一个的反照；一个是外在处境的完全规定性和界限的长廊，另一个则是把同一个东西翻译成它们在意识本质中存在的方式；前者是球面，后者是把球面表象在自身之内的中心点。

en: But the spherical surface, the world of the individual, has immediately the ambiguous meaning of being world and situation existing in and for itself, and world of the individual either in so far as the latter would merely have flowed together with it, let it enter into itself as it is, and behaved toward it only as formal consciousness – or else of being the world of the individual as what is at hand has been inverted by it.

– Since by virtue of this freedom actuality is capable of this double meaning, the world of the individual is to be comprehended only out of this individual itself, and the influence of the actuality that is represented as existing in and for itself upon the individual receives through the latter absolutely the opposite sense, namely that it either lets the stream of inflowing actuality have its way with it or that it cuts it off and inverts it.
But thereby psychological necessity becomes so empty a word that, of what is supposed to have had this influence, there is the absolute possibility that it also could not have had it.
zh: 但是，球面、即个体的世界，直接就有这样一种双重的意义：它既是自在自为地存在着的世界和状况，又是个体的世界——要么是这样：个体与它只是交融在一起，让它如其所是地进入自己之内，并且对它只表现为形式意识；——要么是那样：它是这样一个个体的世界，即现成存在的东西已被这个个体颠倒过来了。
——既然由于这种自由，现实性能够具有这种双重的意义，那么个体的世界就只能从个体自身出发去以概念把握，而被表象为自在自为地存在着的现实性对个体的影响，通过个体绝对地获得了相反的意义：个体要么听任涌入的现实性之流在它身上施展，要么把这一洪流切断并颠倒过来。
但这样一来，心理学的必然性就变成了一个如此空洞的词，以至于对于据说曾有过这种影响的东西，绝对有可能它本来也可以没有这种影响。

en: Therewith the being falls away that would be in and for itself and was to make up the one, and indeed the universal, side of a law.

Individuality is what its world is as its own; it is itself the circle of its doing, in which it has presented itself as actuality, and absolutely only the unity of the being at hand and the being made; a unity whose sides do not fall apart, as in the representation of the psychological law, into a world existing in itself and an individuality existing for itself; or if they are thus considered each for itself, then no necessity and law of their relation to one another is present.
zh: 这样一来，那种自在自为地存在、并且应当构成一条规律的其中一面、而且是普遍的那一面的存在，就消失不见了。
个体性就是它的世界作为它自己的世界所是的那个东西；它自己就是它的行动的圆圈，在其中它把自己展现为现实性，并且绝对只是现成存在的存在与被造成的存在之统一；这种统一的各个方面并不像在心理学规律的表象中那样，分崩为自在存在着的世界和自为存在着的个体性；或者，如果它们被这样各自分开来看，那么它们彼此之间的关系就没有任何必然性和规律。

12.en: c. Observation of the Relation of Self-Consciousness to its Immediate Actuality; Physiognomy and Phrenology
12.zh: c. 对自我意识与其直接现实性的关系的观察；面相学和颅相学

en: Psychological observation finds no law of the relation of self-consciousness to actuality or to the world opposed to it and is driven back, by the indifference of the two to one another, to the peculiar determinacy of the real individuality, which is in and for itself, or contains the opposition of being-for-itself and being-in-itself cancelled in their absolute mediation.
It is the object that has now become the object of observation, or to which observation passes over.
zh: 心理学的观察找不到自我意识与现实性、或与和它相对立的世界之间关系的规律，并且由于两者彼此漠不相关，它被逼回到实在的个体性那种特有的规定性上去，这种个体性是自在自为的，或者说，它把自为存在与自在存在的对立在其绝对中介中消除掉而包含于自身。
它就是现在已成为观察之对象的那个对象，或者说，是观察所过渡到的那个对象。

en: The individual is in and for itself: it is for itself, or it is a free doing; but it is also in itself, or it itself has an original determinate being – a determinacy that according to the concept is the same as what psychology wanted to find outside it.
In it itself, therefore, the opposition emerges, this doubledness: to be movement of consciousness and the firm being of an appearing actuality, of such an actuality as is immediately its own in it.
This being, the body of the determinate individuality, is the originality of the latter, its not-having-done.

But since the individual is at the same time only what it has done, its body is also the expression of itself that it has brought forth; at the same time a sign that has not remained an immediate matter, but in which it only gives to be cognized what it is in the sense that it directs its original nature into the work.
zh: 个体是自在自为的：它是自为的，或者说它是一种自由的行为；但它也是自在的，或者说它自身具有一种原初的、确定的存在——一种按照概念来说与心理学想在它之外找到的东西相同的规定性。
所以在它自身上就出现了这种对立、这种双重性：既是意识的运动，又是一种显现着的现实性的坚固存在，而这种现实性在它身上直接就是它自己的现实性。
这种存在，即确定个体性的身体，是这种个体性的原初性，是它的未曾有所做。
但是，既然个体同时只是它所做过的事情，那么它的身体也是由它产生出来的、它自己的表达；同时是一个符号，这个符号并没有停留在直接的事情上，而它在这个符号上只是让人认识到它是什么，其意义是：它把自己的原初本性付诸实现。

en: If we consider the moments present here in relation to the preceding view, what we have here is a universal human shape, or at least the universal shape of a climate, a part of the world, a people, just as before [we had] the same universal customs and culture.
To these are added the particular circumstances and situation within the universal actuality; here this particular actuality is [there] as the particular formation of the shape of the individual.

— On the other side, just as before the free doing of the individual and the actuality as its own were posited over against the existing [actuality], here the shape stands as the expression of its realization posited through itself, the traits and forms of its self-active essence.

But the actuality that is both universal and particular, which observation previously found outside the individual, is here the actuality of the same, its innate body, and it is precisely into this that the expression falls which belongs to its doing.

In the psychological consideration, the actuality that is in and for itself and the determinate individuality were to be related to one another; here, however, the whole determinate individuality is the object of observation; and each side of its opposition is itself this whole.

To the outer whole there thus belongs not only the original being, the innate body, but equally its formation, which belongs to the activity of the inner; it is the unity of unformed and of formed being, and the actuality of the individual permeated by being-for-itself.

This whole, which contains in itself the determinate original firm parts and the traits that arise solely through doing, is, and this being is the expression of the inner, of the individual posited as consciousness and movement.

— This inner is likewise no longer the formal, contentless or indeterminate self-activity whose content and determinacy, as before, would lie in the outer circumstances, but it is an in-itself determinate original character whose form is only activity.
Between these two sides, then, the relation is here considered, how it is to be determined and what is to be understood by this expression of the inner in the outer.
zh: 如果我们联系先前的看法来考察这里现成的各个环节，那么这里就是一种普遍的人的形态，或者至少是一个气候、一个大洲、一个民族的普遍形态，正如先前是那些同样的普遍习俗和教养。
除此之外，还有普遍现实性之内的那些特殊环境和处境；在这里，这种特殊的现实性就是作为个体形态的特殊构形。
——在另一方面，正如先前个体的自由行动和作为它自己的现实性被设定为与现成的现实性相对立，在这里，形态就是它通过自身设定的现实化的表达，是它自己活动着的本质的那些特征和形式。
但是，那种既普遍又特殊的现实性——观察先前在个体之外发现了它——在这里就是这个个体自己的现实性，就是它天生的身体，而属于它行动的那种表达恰恰落在其中。
在心理学的考察里，自在自为地存在着的现实性和特定的个体性应当被相互关联起来；但在这里，整个特定的个体性都是观察的对象；而它这个对立的每一方自身就是这个整体。
所以，属于外在整体的不仅有原初的存在、即天生的身体，而且同样有这身体的构形，而这种构形属于内在东西的活动；它是未成形的存在和已成形的存在的统一，是被自为存在贯穿了的个体之现实性。
这个整体——它把那些特定的、原初的、固定的部分和那些仅仅通过行动才产生的特征都包含在自身之中——存在着，而这种存在就是内在东西的表达，就是那个被设定为意识和运动的个体的表达。
——这个内在东西同样不再是那种形式的、无内容的或不确定的自身活动，这种活动的内容和规定性会像先前那样落在外部环境里，而是一个自在地被规定的、原初的性格，它的形式只是活动。
所以，这里要考察的是这两方之间的关系：它该如何规定，以及在这种内在东西在外在东西中的表达之下该理解什么。

en: This outer makes the inner visible at first only as organ, or [makes it] into a being for another in general; for the inner, insofar as it is in the organ, is activity itself.

The speaking mouth, the working hand, and if one likes the legs as well, are the realizing and accomplishing organs that have doing as doing, or the inner as such, on them; but the externality that it gains through them is the deed as an actuality separated from the individual.
Speech and work are expressions in which the individual no longer keeps and possesses itself on itself, but lets the inner come wholly outside itself and gives it over to another.

One can therefore say just as much that these expressions express the inner too much as that they express it too little; too much — because the inner itself breaks out in them, no opposition remains between them and it; they give not only an expression of the inner but the inner itself immediately; too little — because the inner in speech and action makes itself into another, it thereby gives itself over to the element of transformation, which turns the spoken word and the accomplished deed around and makes something other out of them than they are in and for themselves as actions of this determinate individual.

Not only do the works of actions lose, through this externality from the influence of others, the character of being something lasting over against other individualities; but in that they comport themselves toward the inner that they contain as a separated, indifferent outer, they can, as inner, through the individual itself, be something other than they appear — either that it deliberately makes them, for the sake of appearance, into something other than they truly are, or that it is too clumsy to give itself the outward side that it actually wanted and to fix it in such a way that its work cannot be turned around by others.

Doing, then, as accomplished work, has the double, opposed meaning of being either the inner individuality and not its expression, or, as outer, an actuality free of the inner, which is something wholly other than the former.
— On account of this ambiguity we must look around for the inner as it still is on the individual itself, though visibly or externally.
In the organ, however, it is only as immediate doing itself, which attains its externality in the deed, which either represents the inner or does not.
The organ, considered under this opposition, thus does not yield the expression that is sought.
zh: 这种外在东西最初只是作为器官才让内在东西变得可见，或者一般地把内在东西变成一种为他存在；因为内在东西，只要它在器官之中，它就是活动本身。
说话的嘴、劳动的手，如果人们愿意，还可以加上腿，都是实现着和完成着的器官，它们身上拥有作为行动的行动、或者说拥有内在东西本身；但它通过它们所获得的外在性，则是作为与个体分离开来的现实性的行为。
语言和劳动是表现，在其中个体不再在自身那里保持和拥有自己，而是让内在东西完全来到自身之外，并把它交给另一个。

因此，人们同样可以说这些表现把内在东西表达得太多，也可以说它们把它表达得太少；太多——因为内在东西本身在它们之中爆发出来，它们与它之间就不剩下任何对立；它们给出的不只是内在东西的一种表达，而是直接给出内在东西本身；太少——因为内在东西在语言和行动中把自己变成一个他者，它就由此把自己交给变化的元素，这种元素把说出的词和完成了的行为颠倒过来，使它们变成不同于它们作为这个特定个体的行动而自在自为所是的东西。
行动的作品不仅由于这种出自其他东西的作用的外在性而失去那种相对于其他个体性而言是持存之物的性格；而且，由于它们对自己所包含的内在东西采取一种分离的、漠不相关的外在东西的态度，它们作为内在东西就可能通过个体本身而不同于它们所显现的样子——要么是个体有意为了现象把它们弄成不同于它们在真理中所是的东西，要么是它太笨拙，无法给自己提供它本来想要的外在方面，也无法把它固定下来，使别人不能颠倒它的作品。
所以，行动作为完成了的作品，具有双重的、相反的含义：要么是内在的个体性而不是它的表达，要么作为外在东西而是一种不依赖于内在东西的现实性，这种现实性完全是另一个东西，不同于那个内在东西。
——由于这种歧义，我们必须回过头去寻找内在东西，看它如何还——但以可见的或外在的方式——在个体自身那里。
但在器官里，它只是作为直接的行动本身，而行动在行为中获得自己的外在性，这种行为要么把内在东西表象出来，要么不表象出来。
所以，就这种对立来看，器官并不提供那种被寻找的表达。

en: If, now, the outer shape could express the inner individuality only insofar as it is not organ or not doing, and thus as a resting whole, then it would comport itself as an existing thing that quietly received the inner as something foreign into its passive determinate being and thereby became its sign; — an outer, contingent expression whose actual side is in itself meaningless, — a language whose tones and combinations of tones are not the matter itself but are linked with it by free caprice and are contingent for it.
zh: 如果外在形态只能就它不是器官或不是行动、因而是一个静止的整体而言才能表达内在的个体性，那么它就会像一个现成存在着的物那样行事：这个物把内在东西当作一个陌生的东西平静地接进自己的被动定在之中，并由此成为内在东西的标志；——这是一种外在的、偶然的表达，它的现实的一面自为地是无意义的，——这是一种语言，它的音以及音的组合并不是事情本身，而是通过自由的任意与事情本身联结起来、对事情本身而言是偶然的。

en: Such an arbitrary connection of things that are an outer for one another gives no law.

Physiognomy is, however, supposed to distinguish itself from other bad arts and pernicious studies by this, that it considers the determinate individuality in the necessary opposition of an inner and an outer, of the character as conscious essence and of the very same as existing shape, and relates these moments to one another as they are related to one another through their concept and must therefore constitute the content of a law.
In astrology, chiromancy and similar sciences, by contrast, only an outer seems to be related to an outer, some thing to something foreign to it.

This constellation at birth and, if this outer is brought closer to the body itself, these traits of the hand are outer moments for the long or short life and the fate of the single human being in general.
As externalities they comport themselves indifferently toward one another and do not have for one another the necessity that is supposed to lie in the relation of an outer and an inner.
zh: 这样一些彼此互为外在东西的东西之间的这种任意联结，并不给出任何规律。
但面相学据说应当以这一点与其他糟糕的技艺和有害的研究区分开来：它在内在东西与外在东西、在作为有意识的本质的性格与作为存在着的形态的同一个性格之间那种必然的对立中考察特定的个体性，并且这样把这些环节相互关联起来，如同它们通过自己的概念而相互关联、因而必须构成一条规律的内容那样。
与此相反，在星象学、手相术以及诸如此类的学问里，似乎只有外在东西与外在东西、某个东西与一个对它陌生的东西被关联起来。
出生时的这个星位，以及——如果把这种外在东西更近地挪到身体本身上来——手上的这些特征，对于单个的人一般而言生命的或长或短和他的命运来说，都是外在的环节。
作为外在的东西，它们彼此漠不相关，并不具有那种应当在一种外在东西与内在东西的关联中存在的、对彼此而言的必然性。

en: The hand, to be sure, seems to be not so much something outer for fate, but rather to comport itself toward it as inner.
For fate is again only the appearance of what the determinate individuality is in itself as inner, original determinacy.

— To know what it is in itself, the chiromancer as well as the physiognomist arrives at in a shorter way than, for instance, Solon, who thought he could know this only from and after the course of a whole life; he considered the appearance, but those consider the in-itself.

But that the hand must present the in-itself of individuality with regard to its fate is easy to see from this, that next to the organ of speech it is most of all that through which the human being brings himself to appearance and realization.

It is the ensouled master-craftsman of his fortune; one can say of it that it is what the human being does, for on it, as the active organ of his self-accomplishment, he is present as ensouling, and since he is originally his own fate, it will thus express this in-itself.
zh: 诚然，手看起来并不那么是某种对命运而言的外在东西，反而更像是作为内在东西而与命运发生关联。
因为命运同样只是那个东西的现象：特定的个体性自在地作为内在的、原初的规定性所是的东西。
——要知道它自在地是什么，手相师和面相学家所用的方式比例如梭伦要短；梭伦认为只有从整个生命的进程中、并且在这之后才能知道这一点；梭伦考察的是现象，而他们考察的却是自在。
但手必须把个体性在其命运方面的自在呈现出来，这一点很容易看出，因为除语言的器官之外，它最是人借以把自己带到现象和现实化之中的那种东西。
它是他的幸运的有灵魂的工匠；人们可以说，它就是人所做的东西，因为在他自我完成的活动器官即手上，他作为赋予灵魂者是在场的，而既然他原初地就是他自己的命运，那么手就会把这种自在表达出来。

en: From this determination, that the organ of activity is just as much a being as the doing in it, or that the inner being-in-itself is itself present on it and has a being for others, there results a different view of it than the previous one.

For if the organs in general showed themselves to be incapable of being taken as expressions of the inner, because in them the doing as doing is present, but the doing as deed is only something external, and inner and outer in this way fall apart and are or can be alien to each other, then according to the determination under consideration the organ must again be taken as the middle of both, in that precisely this, that the doing is present on it, at the same time constitutes an externality of it, and indeed one different from the deed; for the former remains for the individual and on it.

– This middle and unity of inner and outer is now, first, itself also external; but then this externality is at the same time taken up into the inner; as simple externality it stands opposed to the dispersed externality, which is either only a single work or state contingent for the whole individuality, or else, as whole externality, is the fate shattered into a multiplicity of works and states.

The simple features of the hand, then, and likewise the sound and range of the voice as the individual determinacy of language – also the same again as through the hand it obtains a firmer existence than through the voice, namely writing, and indeed in its particularity as handwriting – all this is expression of the inner, so that it as simple externality again relates itself to the manifold externality of acting and of fate, relates itself as inner to these.

– If, then, first the determinate nature and innate peculiarity of the individual, together with what they have become through formation, is taken as the inner, as the essence of acting and of fate, then it has its appearance and externality first on its mouth, hand, voice, handwriting, as well as on the other organs and their abiding determinacies; and only then does it further express itself outward on its actuality in the world.
zh: 从这一规定——活动的器官既是一种存在，又是在它之中的行动，或者说，内在的自在存在本身就在它上面在场，并且有一种为他存在——产生出关于它的另一种看法，不同于先前的看法。
因为，如果器官之所以根本不能被当作内在东西的表达，是因为在它们之中，行动作为行动是在场的，而行动作为行为却只是外在的东西，并且内在东西和外在东西以这种方式彼此分离、互为异己或可能互为异己，那么按照所考察的这一规定，器官也必须重新被当作两者的中项，因为正是这一点——行动在它上面在场——同时构成了它的一种外在性，而且是不同于行为的那种外在性；也就是说，前者为个体所保留，并且就在个体身上。
——这个内在东西和外在东西的中项和统一，首先本身也是外在的；但其次，这种外在性同时又被收进内在东西之中；它作为简单的外在性而与那种分散的外在性相对立，后者要么只是一个单个的、对整个个体性来说偶然的作品或状态，要么作为整体的外在性，就是那个分裂为众多作品和状态的命运。
所以，手的那些简单特征，以及声音的音色和音域作为语言的那种个体性的规定性——此外还有语言本身，即它通过手而获得一种比通过声音更稳固的存在，也就是文字，而且是在它作为笔迹的特殊性中——所有这一切都是内在东西的表达，以至于它作为简单的外在性又同行动和命运的多种多样的外在性相对待，作为内在东西则同这些外在性相对待。
——所以，如果首先把个体特定的本性和天生的特性、连同它们通过教养所成为的东西，当作内在东西、当作行动和命运的本质，那么它的现象和外在性首先就在它的嘴、手、声音、笔迹以及其余器官和这些器官持存的规定性上；然后它才进一步在它于世界中的现实性上向外表达自己。

en: Since now this middle determines itself as the expression that is at the same time taken back into the inner, its determinate being is not restricted to the immediate organ of the doing; it is rather the movement and form of the face and of shaping in general that accomplishes nothing.

These features and their movement are, according to this concept, the retained doing that remains on the individual, and, according to its relation to the actual doing, the individual's own supervising and observing of the same, expression as reflection on the actual expression.

– The individual is therefore not silent in and at its outer doing, because it is at the same time reflected into itself therein, and it expresses this being-reflected-into-itself; this theoretical doing, or the individual's language with itself about it, is also audible for others, for it is itself an expression.
zh: 既然这个中项把自己规定为那种同时被收回内在东西之中的表现，那么它的定在就不被限制在行动的那个直接器官上；它毋宁是脸部和一般形态塑造的那种不成就任何东西的运动和形式。
这些特征及其运动，按照这个概念，就是那种被扣留住的、停留在个体身上的行动，而按照它同现实行动的关系，就是个体自己对这种现实行动的监督和观察，是作为对现实表现进行反思的表现。
——个体在从事自己的外在行动、并身处其中时之所以不是沉默的，是因为它同时在其中反思回自身，并且它把这种在自身中的反思表现出来；这种理论性的行动，或者说个体就这件事同自己交谈的语言，对别人来说也是听得见的，因为它本身就是一种表现。

en: On this inner, which in its expression remains inner, the being-reflected of the individual out of its actuality is therefore observed, and it is to be seen how matters stand with this necessity that is posited in this unity.

– This being-reflected is at first different from the deed itself and can therefore be something else and be taken for something else than it is; one can see from a person's face whether he is in earnest about what he says or does.

– Conversely, however, this, which is supposed to be expression of the inner, is at the same time an existent expression and thereby itself falls down into the determination of being, which is absolutely contingent for the self-conscious essence.
It is therefore indeed expression, but at the same time also only like a sign, so that the constitution of that whereby it is expressed is completely indifferent to the expressed content.
The inner is in this appearance indeed a visible invisible, but without being tied to it; it can just as well be in another appearance, as another inner can be in the same appearance.
– Lichtenberg therefore says with reason: 'Suppose the physiognomist ever caught a human being, it would only take an honest resolve to make oneself incomprehensible again for millennia.'

– As in the preceding relation the circumstances at hand were a being out of which individuality took for itself what it was capable of and wanted, either surrendering itself to it or perverting it, on which ground it did not contain the necessity and the essence of individuality, – so here the appearing immediate being of individuality is such that it either expresses its being-reflected out of actuality and its being-within-itself, or is for it only a sign that is indifferent to what is designated and therefore in truth designates nothing; it is for it just as much its face as its mask, which it can lay aside.

– It pervades its shape, moves, speaks in it; but this whole determinate being likewise steps over as a being indifferent to the will and the action; it erases on it the meaning it previously had, of having its being-reflected into itself or its true essence on it, and conversely rather lays it into the will and into the deed.
zh: 在这个于其表现中仍然是内在东西的内在东西上，人们于是观察个体从它的现实性中的反思，并且要看看，那种被设定在这种统一之中的必然性，情形究竟怎样。
——这种反思首先不同于行为本身，因此它可以是别的东西，也可以被当作不同于行为的东西；人们从一个人脸上就看得出来，他对自己所说或所做的，是不是认真的。
——但反过来，这种应当是内在东西之表达的东西，同时又是存在着的表达，并因此本身跌落到存在的规定里，而存在对自我意识着的本质来说是绝对偶然的。
因此它固然是表达，但同时也不过像一个记号，以至于对那个被表达出来的内容来说，用以表达它的那个东西的状况是完全无关紧要的。
内在东西在这种现象中固然是可看见的不可见者，但并没有系缚在它上面；它同样可以在另一种现象中，正如另一种内在东西可以在同一种现象中一样。
——所以利希滕贝格说得有道理：“假定面相学家有一次逮住了人，那也只需要一个正直的决心，就能让自己在数千年里重新变得不可理解。”

——正如在先前那种关系里，眼前的各种情况是一种存在者，个体性从中取走它所能取、所愿取的东西，要么顺从它，要么颠倒它，正因如此，它并不包含个体性的必然性和本质——同样，在这里，个体性那种显现着的直接存在也是这样一种东西：它要么表达出个体性从现实性中的反思和它的自身内存在，要么对个体性来说只是一个记号，这个记号对被标记的东西无关紧要，因此真正说来什么也没有标记；它既是个体性的脸，又是个体性可以摘下的面具。
——它贯穿自己的形态，在其中运动、说话；但这整个定在同样作为一种对意志和行动无关紧要的存在而出现；它抹掉了它在这个定在上先前具有的那种含义，即在这个定在上拥有自己在自身中的反思或自己真正的本质，反而把这含义放进意志和行为里。

en: Individuality gives up that being-reflected-into-itself which is expressed in the features, and lays its essence into the work.

Herein it contradicts the relation that is fixed by the instinct of reason, which applies itself to the observing of self-conscious individuality, with regard to what is supposed to be its inner and its outer.
This point of view leads us to the proper thought that lies at the basis of the physiognomic – if one will – science.

The opposition into which this observation falls is, as to form, the opposition of the practical and the theoretical, both namely posited within the practical itself, – of the individuality that actualizes itself in acting (this taken in the most universal sense) and of the same individuality as it in this acting is at the same time out of it, reflected into itself, and this acting is its object.
Observation takes up this opposition according to the same inverted relation in which it determines itself in the appearance.
For the unessential outer, the deed itself and the work count for it, be it of language or of a more fixed actuality, – but for the essential inner, the being-within-itself of individuality.

Among the two sides that practical consciousness has on it, the intending and the deed – the meaning about its action and the action itself – observation chooses that side as the true inner; this is to have its more or less unessential expression in the deed, but its true one in its shape.

The latter expression is the immediate sensuous presentness of the individual spirit; the inwardness that is supposed to be the true one is the peculiarity of the intention and the singularity of being-for-itself; both are the meant spirit.
What observation has as its objects is therefore meant determinate being, and among such it seeks for laws.
zh: 个体性放弃了那种在特征中表达出来的、在自身中的反思，而把它的本质放进作品里。
在这里，它与那种关系相矛盾，这种关系是由那个致力于观察自我意识着的个体性的理性本能，就什么应当是个体性的内在东西和外在东西这一点而确立起来的。
这个观点把我们引向那个真正的思想，它——如果人们愿意这么说的话——是面相学的科学的根据。
这种观察所陷入的对立，在形式上就是实践的东西和理论的东西的对立，不过两者都被设定在实践的东西本身之内，——也就是在行动中（这要在最普遍的意义上来理解）实现自身的个体性，与同一个个体性之间的对立，后者在这种行动中同时从中走出、反思回自身，而行动则是它的对象。
观察按照这种对立在现象中规定自己所依据的那种同样的颠倒关系，来接纳这种对立。
在它看来，行为本身和作品——不管是语言的，还是一种更固定下来的现实性——算作非本质的外在东西，而个体性的自身内存在则算作本质性的内在东西。
在实践意识于它身上所具有的两个方面——意图和行为，即关于自己行动的意谓和行动本身——之中，观察把前一个方面选作真的内在东西；这个内在东西应当把它的或多或少非本质的表现放在行为上，而把它的真的表现放在它的形态上。
后一种表现是个体精神的直接的感性当前在场；那种应当是真正的内在性，是意图的独特性以及自为存在的个别性；两者都是被意谓的精神。
所以，观察当作自己对象的东西，是被意谓的定在，而它就是在这样的东西之间去寻找规律。

en: The immediate opinion about the meant presence of spirit is natural physiognomy, the hasty judgment about the inner nature and the character of its shape at first sight of it.
The object of this opinion is of such a kind that it lies in its essence to be in truth something other than only sensuous immediate being.
To be sure, it is likewise precisely this being-reflected-into-itself out of the sensuous, what is present, the visibility as visibility of the invisible, that is the object of observation.

But precisely this sensuous immediate presence is actuality of spirit as it is only for opinion; and in this respect observation turns around with its meant determinate being, with the physiognomy, handwriting, tone of the voice, and so on.
– It relates such determinate being to just such a meant inner [element].

It is not the murderer, the thief, that is to be recognized, but the capacity to be it; the firm abstract determinacy thereby loses itself in the concrete infinite determinacy of the single individual, which now requires more artful portrayals than those qualifications are.

Such artful portrayals indeed say more than the qualification through murderer, thief, or good-hearted, uncorrupted, and so on, but for their purpose, to express the meant being or the single individuality, far from enough, as little as the portrayals of the shape which go beyond the flat forehead, long nose, and so on.
For the single shape as well as the single self-consciousness is, as meant being, inexpressible.

The science of knowledge of human beings, which goes after the supposed human being, as well as [the science] of physiognomy, which goes after its supposed actuality and wants to raise the unconscious judging of natural physiognomy to a knowing, is therefore something endless and bottomless, which can never get to say what it means, because it only means and its content is only something meant.
zh: 关于精神的被意谓的在场的直接意谓，就是自然的面相学，就是对它的形态的内在自然和性格在第一眼看到它时作出的仓促判断。
这种意谓的对象是这样一种东西：它的本质就在于，它其实是某种别的，而不只是感性的直接存在。
当然，正是这个在感性之物中从它出发反思回自身的存在，正是这个在场的东西，这个作为不可见者的可见性的可见性，才是观察的对象。
但正是这种感性的直接的在场，才是精神的现实性，而它只是对意谓而言才如此；观察在这一方面就带着它那被意谓的定在团团打转，琢磨着面相、笔迹、声音的声调等等。
——它把这样的定在联系到同样被意谓的内在。
要认识的并不是凶手、小偷，而是能够成为凶手、小偷的那种能力；固定的抽象的规定性由此消融在单个个体的具体的无限规定性之中，而这种规定性现在要求比那些资格鉴定更需要技巧的描绘。
这样一些需要技巧的描绘，固然比用凶手、小偷，或者好心肠、没变坏等等所作的资格鉴定说得更多，但就它们的目的——说出那被意谓的存在或单个的个体性——来说，却远远不够，正如超出平坦的额头、长鼻子等等的形态描绘也远远不够一样。
因为单个的形态和单个的自我意识一样，作为被意谓的存在都是不可言说的。
所以，关于人的知识这门科学既然着眼于那被设想的人，面相学既然着眼于他自以为的现实性，并且想把自然的面相学那种无意识的判断提升为一种知识，它们就都是无穷无尽、没有根基的东西，永远无法进到说出自己所意谓的东西，因为它只是在意谓，而它的内容只是被意谓的东西。

en: The laws that this science sets out to find are relations of these two meant sides and can therefore themselves be nothing but an empty meaning.

Since, moreover, this meant knowing, which sets about dealing with the actuality of spirit, has precisely this as its object, that spirit reflects itself out of its sensuous determinate being into itself, and that the determinate being is for it an indifferent contingency, it must immediately know, with the laws it has found, that nothing is thereby said, but that in fact there is pure idle chatter or only a meaning is given about itself; an expression that has the truth of stating this as the same thing – to say its meaning and thereby bring forward not the matter but only a meaning about itself.
As regards content, however, these observations cannot differ from those: “It always rains when we have a fair, says the merchant; and always, too, when I dry my laundry, says the housewife.”
zh: 这门科学要去找的那些规律，是被意谓的这两个方面之间的关系，所以它们本身只能是一种空洞的意谓。
而且，既然这种意谓着的知识着手与精神的现实性打交道，却恰恰把这一点当作自己的对象：精神从它的感性定在中反思回自身，并且这特定的定在对它来说是一种无关紧要的偶然性，那么它带着自己找出来的那些规律，就必定直接知道：借此什么也没有说出，而实际上是纯粹在闲扯，或者只是说出了关于自己的一种意谓；这个说法有一种真理，就是把这一点说成同一回事——说出自己的意谓，并借此带来的不是事情，而只是关于自己的一种意谓。
在内容上，这些观察却不可能与下面这些有什么不同：“我们一有集市，天就总是下雨，商人说；我一晾衣服，天也总是下雨，家庭主妇说。”

en: Lichtenberg, who characterizes physiognomic observation in this way, also says this: “If someone said: you do indeed act like an honest man, but I see from your figure that you are forcing yourself and are a rogue in your heart; truly such an address will to the end of the world be answered by every honest fellow with a box on the ear.”
– This reply is to the point because it is the refutation of the first presupposition of such a science of meaning, namely that the actuality of the human being is his face and so on.
– The true being of the human being is rather his deed; in it individuality is actual, and it is this that sublates what is meant in both its sides.
First, what is meant as a bodily resting being; individuality presents itself in the action rather as the negative essence, which is only insofar as it sublates being.
Then the deed sublates the inexpressibility of the meaning just as much with regard to the self-conscious individuality, which in the meaning is an infinitely determinate and determinable one.
In the accomplished deed this bad infinity is destroyed.
The deed is a simply determinate [content], universal, to be grasped in an abstraction; it is murder, theft, or benefaction, a brave deed, and so on, and it can be said of it what it is.
It is this, and its being is not only a sign but the matter itself.
It is this, and the individual human being is what it is; in the simplicity of this being he is a being-for-others, universal essence and ceases to be only something meant.

To be sure, he is not posited therein as spirit; but since there is talk of his being as being, and on the one hand the doubled being, that of the shape and that of the deed, stand opposed to each other, and the former as well as the latter is supposed to be his actuality, then rather only the deed is to be asserted as his genuine being – not his figure, which was supposed to express what he means by his deeds, or what one meant that he could only do.

Likewise, since on the other hand his work and his inner possibility, capacity or intention are opposed, the former alone is to be regarded as his true actuality, even if he himself is deceived about it and, turned back into himself out of his action, means to be something other in this inner [realm] than in the deed.
Individuality that entrusts itself to the objective element by becoming a work thereby indeed gives itself over to being changed and perverted.
But precisely this constitutes the character of the deed: whether it is a real being that sustains itself, or only a meant work that passes away as null in itself.
Objectivity does not change the deed itself but only shows what it is, i.e. whether it is or whether it is nothing.

– The dissection of this being into intentions and similar refinements, by which the actual human being, i.e. his deed, is again to be explained back into a meant being, just as he himself may well also create for himself particular intentions about his actuality, must be left to the idleness of meaning, which, when it wants to set its deedless wisdom to work, wants to deny the character of reason in the one who acts and to maltreat him in such a way that, instead of the deed, it wants to declare the figure and the features to be the being of the same, [and thus] has to fear the above reply, which shows it that the figure is not the in-itself but can rather be an object of treatment.
zh: 利希滕贝格这样刻画面相学的观察，他还说了这样的话：“假如有人说：你行事倒像个老实人，但我从你的体形看出来，你是在强迫自己，心里是个无赖；说真的，这样一句招呼，直到世界末日都会被每个正派家伙用一个耳光来回答。”
——这个回答之所以切中要害，是因为它驳倒了这样一种意谓的科学的第一条前提，即：人的现实性就是他的脸等等。
——人的真正存在反倒是他的行为；在行为中个体性是现实的，而正是行为扬弃了被意谓的东西的两个方面。
一方面，被意谓的东西作为身体性的、静止的存在；个体性在行动中反倒表现为否定的本质，它只在扬弃存在时才存在。
其次，行为同样在对自我意识的个体性方面扬弃了意谓的不可言说性，这种个体性在意谓中是一种无限地规定了的、可无限规定的个体性。
在完成了的行为中，这种坏的无限被消灭了。
行为是一种单纯被规定的东西、普遍的东西，要在一种抽象中把握；它是谋杀、偷窃或者善行、勇敢的行为等等，关于它可以说出它是什么。
它就是这，而它的存在不只是一个符号，而是事情本身。
它就是这，而个体的人就是这行为所是的东西；在这种存在的单纯性中，他是为他的、普遍的本质，并且不再是单纯被意谓的东西。
诚然，他在其中并不是被设定为精神；但既然谈的是他的存在之为存在，而且一方面是形态和行为这二重化的存在互相对立，并且前者和后者都应当是他的现实性，那么相反，只有行为才应当被断定为他的真正的存在，——不是他的体形，体形应当表达出他对于自己的行为所意谓的东西，或者人们意谓他仅仅能够做出的事情。
同样，既然另一方面他的作品和他的内在可能性、能力或意图被对立起来，那么只有前者才应被看作他真正的现实性，即便他自己在这一点上欺骗自己，并且从自己的行为中返回到自身之内，在内心里意谓自己是另一个样子，不同于在行为中的样子。
把自己托付给对象性要素、从而成为作品的个体性，由此当然就交付出去，任自己被改变、被颠倒。
但恰恰是这一点构成了行为的性格：它是一个自身持存的现实的存在，还是只是一个自身内无谓地消逝的被意谓的作品。
对象性并不改变行为本身，而只是显示出它是什么，也就是说，它存在还是不存在。

——把这种存在分解成意图以及诸如此类的精细东西，借此把现实的人，也就是他的行为，又重新解释回一种被意谓的存在，正如他自己也尽可以就自己的现实性给自己造出种种特殊意图，这种事必须留给意谓的闲散去管；这种闲散在它要把自己那没有行为的智慧付诸实行时，就想否认行动者身上的理性性格，并且用这样一种方式来虐待他：它要取代行为而把体形和相貌特征说成是他的存在，因此它就不得不担心上面那个回答，那个回答向它表明：体形并不是自在，反倒可以成为一个处理的对象。

en: If we now look at the compass of the relations in general in which self-conscious individuality can be observed as standing in relation to its outer, then one relation will remain over which observation must still make its object.
In psychology it is the outer actuality of things that is supposed to have on spirit its self-conscious counterpart and to make spirit intelligible.
In physiognomy, by contrast, spirit is to be cognized in its own outer as in a being that is the language — the visible invisibility — of its essence.
There still remains the determination of the side of actuality, namely that individuality expresses its essence on its immediate, firm, purely existent actuality.

– This last relation thus differs from the physiognomic one in that the latter is the speaking presence of the individual, which in its acting expression at the same time presents the presence that reflects into itself and contemplates itself, an expression that is itself movement, resting traits that are themselves essentially a mediated being.

In the determination still to be considered, however, the outer is finally a wholly resting actuality, which is not in itself a speaking sign, but, separated from self-conscious movement, presents itself for itself and is as a mere thing.
zh: 如果我们现在来看各种关系本身的范围，即自我意识的个体性在其中能够被观察为与自己的外在东西相对而立的那种范围，那么还会剩下一种关系，观察必须把它也当作自己的对象。
在心理学里，正是物的外在现实性应当在精神身上拥有自己意识到自身的对应图像，并使精神变得可以理解。
与此相反，在面相学里，精神则应当在它自己的外在东西中被认识，即被认识为一种存在，而这种存在是它的本质的语言——即可见的不可见性。
还剩下的是现实性这一方面的规定，即个体性在它直接的、固定的、纯粹定在着的现实性上说出自己的本质。
——所以，这最后一种关系与面相学关系的区别在于：后者是个体的言说着的当前在场，个体在自己行动着的表现中同时把那种在自身中反思着、观看着自己的当前在场展示出来，而这种表现本身就是运动，是静止的特征，这些特征本身本质上是一种被中介的存在。
但在还有待考察的那种规定里，外在东西最终是一种完全静止的现实性，它并非在自身那里就是言说着的符号，而是与自我意识的运动分离开来、自为地呈现出来，并且作为单纯的物而存在。

en: First, with regard to the relation of the inner to this its outer, it is evident that this relation seems to have to be comprehended as a relation of causal connection, since the relation of an in-itself-existing [thing] to another in-itself-existing [thing], as a necessary one, is this relation.
zh: 首先，就内在东西对它的这个外在东西的关系来说，有一点是明白的：这种关系看来必须作为因果联系的关系被以概念把握，因为一个自在存在者对一个自在存在者的关系，作为必然的关系，就是这种关系。

en: For spiritual individuality to have an effect on the body, it must itself be bodily as cause.

But the bodily [element] in which it is as cause is the organ — yet not of the doing against outer actuality, but of the doing of the self-conscious essence in itself, outwardly only against its body; it is not immediately to be seen which these organs can be.
If one thought only of organs in general, then the organ of work in general would easily be at hand, likewise the organ of the sexual drive, and so forth.
But such organs are to be considered as tools or as parts that spirit has as one extreme toward the middle, over against the other extreme, which is an outer object.

Here, however, an organ is understood in which the self-conscious individual, as extreme over against its own actuality opposed to it, maintains itself for itself — not one turned outward at the same time, but one reflected in its action, and on which the side of being is not a being for another.

In the physiognomic relation the organ is indeed also considered as determinate being reflected into itself and speaking of the doing; but this being is an objective one, and the result of physiognomic observation is this, that self-consciousness steps over against precisely this its actuality as against something indifferent.

This indifference disappears in that this being-reflected-into-itself is itself effecting; thereby that determinate being receives a necessary relation to it; but for it to be effecting on the determinate being, it must itself have a being, though not properly an objective one, and it is as this organ that it is to be pointed out.
zh: 既然精神的个体性要对身体产生作用，它作为原因本身就必须是身体性的。
但它在其中作为原因而存在的那种身体性的东西，就是器官，不过并不是针对外在现实性而行动的器官，而是自我意识的本质在自身之中行动的器官，对外则只是针对自己的身体；至于这些器官可能是哪些器官，并不能马上看出来。
如果只想到一般的器官，那么一般劳动的器官就很容易找到，性欲的器官等等也一样。
但这类器官必须被看作工具或部分，精神把它们当作一个极端，用来朝向中项、与另一个极端相对，而另一个极端就是外在的对象。
但这里所理解的是一种器官，自我意识的个体在其中作为极端、相对于它自己的、与它相对立的现实性而自为地保持自己，这种器官并非同时朝向外面的，而是在它的行动中反思着的，并且在这种器官身上，存在这一方面并不是为他存在。
在面相学的关系里，器官虽然也被看作在自身中反思着的、并且言说着行动的定在；但这种存在是一种对象性的存在，而面相学观察的结果就是：自我意识恰恰面对它自己的这种现实性，把它当作某种漠不相关的东西而与之相对而立。
这种漠不相关消失在这一点上：这种自身内反思存在本身是起作用的；由此，那种定在就获得了一种对它的必然关系；但它要对定在起作用，它自己就必须有一种存在，不过并不是真正对象性的存在，而它应当被指出为这种器官。

en: In common life, for example, anger, as such an inner doing, is placed in the liver; Plato even grants it something higher, which according to some is even the highest, namely prophecy or the gift of uttering the holy and eternal unreasonably.1 But the movement that the individual has in the liver, the heart, and so forth, cannot be regarded as its wholly self-reflected movement; rather it is in it in such a way that it is already struck into the body and has an animal determinate being turning out against externality.
zh: 在日常生活中，例如愤怒，作为这样一种内在的行动，被安放在肝脏里；柏拉图甚至给它添了某种更高的东西，按某些人的说法甚至是至高者，即预言或不合道理地说出神圣和永恒的东西的禀赋。1 但个体在肝脏、心脏等等里所具有的运动，不能被看作它完全在自身中反思的运动，相反，它在其中毋宁是这样：这种运动已经被打进它的身体，并且具有一种动物性的、向外朝外在性转过去的定在。

en: The nervous system, by contrast, is the immediate rest of the organic in its movement.

The nerves themselves are indeed again the organs of consciousness already sunk into its direction toward the outside; but brain and spinal cord may be regarded as the immediate presence of self-consciousness that remains in itself — the non-objective presence, the one that also does not go out.
Insofar as the moment of being that this organ has is a being for another, determinate being, it is dead being, no longer the presence of self-consciousness.
But this being-in-itself-itself is, according to its concept, a fluidity in which the circles that are thrown into it immediately dissolve and no difference expresses itself as existent.

Meanwhile, just as spirit itself is not an abstract-simple [thing], but a system of movements in which it distinguishes itself into moments, yet in this distinguishing remains free, and just as it articulates its body in general into various functions and assigns a single part of it to only one, so it can also be represented that the fluid being of its being-in-itself is an articulated one; and it seems that it must be represented in this way, because the being of spirit reflected into itself in the brain is itself again only a middle between its pure essence and its bodily articulation, a middle which herewith, by the nature of both and thus from the side of the latter, must also have the existent articulation again on it.
zh: 与此相反，神经系统则是有机体在其运动中的直接静止。
神经本身虽然又是那种已经沉浸于自己朝向外面的方向的意识的器官；但脑和脊髓却可以被看作自我意识的那种留在自身之中的——非对象性的、也不向外走的——直接的当前在场。
就这种器官所具有的存在环节是一种为他存在、即定在而言，它就是死的存在，不再是自我意识的当前在场。
但这种自身内存在按其概念来说是一种流动性，那些被投进其中的圆圈在其中直接消解，没有任何差别作为存在着的差别表达出来。

不过，正如精神本身并不是一种抽象—单纯的东西，而是一个运动的系统，它在其中把自己区分为各个环节，但在这种区分中本身仍然是自由的；又正如它一般地使自己的身体分化为各不相同的职能，并且使身体的某个单独部分只服务于一种职能，同样也可以表象为：它的在自身内存在的流动的存在是有分节的；而且看来必须这样来表象，因为精神在脑中被反思回自身的存在，本身又只是它的纯粹本质和它的身体分节之间的一个中项，而这个中项因此就两者的本性、从而也就从后者的方面来说，必然也重新在自己身上具有那种存在着的分节。

en: Spiritually organic being has at the same time the necessary side of a resting, subsisting determinate being; the former must step back as the extreme of being-for-itself and have the latter over against it as the other extreme, which is then the object on which the former works as cause.
If now brain and spinal cord are that bodily being-for-itself of spirit, then the skull and the spinal column are the other, separated-off extreme in addition, namely the firm, resting thing.

– But since, when anyone thinks of the proper place of the determinate being of spirit, it is not the back but only the head that occurs to him, we may in the investigation of a knowing such as the present one content ourselves with this ground — not too bad a one for it — in order to restrict this determinate being to the skull.

If the back should occur to someone insofar as knowledge and doing are sometimes partly driven in and partly spurred on by it, this would prove nothing for the claim that the spinal cord must also be taken as an indwelling place of spirit and its column as counterpart determinate being, because it would prove too much; for one can likewise recall that other external ways of getting at the activity of spirit, in order to awaken or to hold it back, are also favoured.

– The spinal column therefore, if one wishes, rightly falls away; and it is constructed just as well as many other teachings of the philosophy of nature that the skull alone, to be sure, does not contain the organs of spirit.

For this was just excluded from the concept of this relation, and the skull was therefore taken on the side of determinate being; or, if one were not permitted to recall the concept of the matter, experience teaches that, just as one sees with the eye as organ, so one does not murder, steal, compose poetry, and so forth, with the skull.
– For this reason, one must also refrain from the expression organ for that meaning of the skull of which there is still to be spoken.

For although one is wont to say that for reasonable people it is not the word that matters but the matter, yet no permission is to be taken from this to designate a matter with a word that does not belong to it; for this is at once clumsiness and deception, which only supposes and pretends not to have the right word, and [which] hides from itself that it in fact lacks the matter, that is, the concept; if this were present, it would also have its right word.
– Here, to begin with, only this has been determined, that, as the brain is the living head, the skull is the caput mortuum.
zh: 精神—有机的存在同时具有一个静止持存的定在这一必然的方面；前者必须作为自为存在的极端退回去，并把后者当作另一个极端与它相对，而后者这时就是那个对象，前者作为原因对它起作用。
既然脑和脊髓是精神的那种身体性的自为存在，那么头颅和脊柱就是另外那个被分离出去的极端，即固定静止的物。
——但是，既然每个人在想到精神定在的真正位置时，想到的都不是背，而只是头，那么在对一种像眼前这样的知识的考察中，我们就可以满足于这个理由——对它来说这理由并不算太糟——，以便把这种定在限制在头颅上。
如果某个人想到背，是因为有时知识和行动也一部分由它被驱入、一部分却由它被促动，那么这对“必须把脊髓也一起当作精神的内在居留之所、把它的脊柱当作对应图像的定在”这一点，恰恰什么也证明不了，因为它证明得太多了；因为人们同样可以想到，为了唤醒或抑制精神的活动，人们还爱用别的外在途径去接近它。
——所以，如果人们愿意，脊柱就理所当然地被略去；而“头颅单独虽然并不包含精神的器官”这一点，和许多别的自然哲学学说一样是构造出来的。
因为这一点刚才已经被排除在这种关系的概念之外，所以头颅才被归到定在这一边；或者，如果人们不可以提醒事情的概念，那么经验反正会教导说：正如人们是用眼睛作为器官来看的，人们也同样不是用头颅去杀人、偷窃、作诗等等的。
——因此，对于头颅的那个还有待谈到的含义，也必须避免使用“器官”这个说法。
因为尽管人们习惯说，对理性的人来说要紧的不是词，而是事情，但由此并不能取得许可，用某个并不属于事情的词去标示事情；因为这既是笨拙又是欺骗，它自以为并假装只是没有找到正确的词，同时却对自己隐瞒了：它实际上缺少事情，也就是缺少概念；如果概念存在，它也就会有自己正确的词。
——这里首先只确定了一点：正如脑是活着的头，头颅则是 caput mortuum。

en: In this dead being, then, the spiritual movements and the determinate modes of the brain would have to give themselves their presentation of outer actuality, which however still attaches to the individual itself.

For the relation of these to it, which as dead being does not have spirit dwelling within itself, what first offers itself is that which was fixed above, the outer and mechanical relation, so that the proper organs — and these are on the brain — press it round here, beat it broad there or flatten it, or however else one may present this influence.

Even as a part of the organism, a living self-formation must indeed be thought in it, as in every bone, so that, considered accordingly, it on its side rather presses the brain and posits its outer limitation; for which, as the harder, it also has the capacity the more readily.

But in that case the same relation would still always remain in the determination of the activity of both over against each other; for whether the skull is the determining or the determined, this would change nothing in the causal connection at all, only that then the skull would be made into the immediate organ of self-consciousness, because in it as cause the side of being-for-itself would be found.
But since being-for-itself as organic liveliness falls into both in the same way, the causal connection between them in fact drops away.

But this further formation of both would hang together in the inner and would be an organic pre-established harmony, which leaves the two sides related to each other free over against each other and leaves each its own shape, to which the shape of the other need not correspond; and all the more the shape and the quality over against each other — as the form of the grape and the taste of the wine are free over against each other.

— But since the determination of being-for-itself falls to the side of the brain, and the determination of determinate being to the side of the skull, a causal connection of the two is also to be posited within the organic unity; a necessary relation of them as external for one another, i.e. a itself external one, whereby their shape would be determined by one another.
zh: 所以，在这种死去的存在里，精神的运动和脑的那些确定的方式就得给自己提供它们对外在现实性的展示，而这种现实性却还附着在个体自己身上。
对于这些同它之间的关系——它作为死去的存在，并不让精神居住在自身之中——，首先呈现出来的就是上面已经确定的那种关系，即外在的、机械的关系，以至于那些真正的器官——而它们是在脑上——在这里把它压圆，在那里把它打宽或压平，或者人们还可以用别的什么方式来展示这种作用。
即使它是有机体的一部分，在它里面也确实必须像在每一块骨头里那样设想一种活生生的自我形成，以至于照此来看，它从自己这方面毋宁说是在压脑，并且设定脑的外在限制；而它作为更硬的东西，也更有能力做到这一点。
但这样一来，在两者相互对立着的活动的规定中，仍然始终会保留同一种关系；因为无论头颅是起规定作用的东西还是被规定的东西，这根本不会改变因果联系，只不过那样一来，头颅就会被弄成自我意识的直接器官，因为在它作为原因的身上会找到自为存在这一方面。
但既然自为存在作为有机的活生生性以同样的方式落在两者身上，它们之间的因果联系实际上就消失了。
但两者各自的这种继续形成却会在内部联结在一起，并且会是一种有机的前定和谐，这种和谐让这两个相互关联的方面彼此自由相对，并让每一方都有自己的形态，而另一方的形态并不需要与之相符；更是让形态和质彼此相对，——就像葡萄粒的形式和葡萄酒的味道彼此自由相对一样。
——但既然自为存在的规定落在脑这一边，而定在的规定落在头颅这一边，那么在有机的统一体内部也就必须设定两者的一种因果联系；即一种它们作为彼此外在的东西的必然关系，也就是说，一种本身外在的关系，由此它们的形态就会通过彼此而被规定。

en: But with regard to the determination in which the organ of self-consciousness would be the active cause over against the opposite side, one can talk back and forth in many ways; for what is at issue is the constitution of a cause that is considered according to its indifferent determinate being, its shape and size, a cause whose inner and being-for-itself is supposed to be precisely such as does not concern the immediate determinate being at all.

The organic self-formation of the skull is at first indifferent to mechanical influence, and the relation of these two relations is, since the former is the relating-to-itself, precisely this indeterminacy and boundlessness itself.

Then, even if the brain were to take up the differences of spirit into itself as existent differences and were a multiplicity of inner organs occupying a different space — which contradicts nature, which gives the moments of the concept a determinate being of their own and therefore places the fluid simplicity of organic life purely on one side and its articulation and division likewise in its differences on the other side, so that they, as they are here to be grasped, show themselves as particular anatomical things —, it would be indeterminate whether a spiritual moment, according as it were originally stronger or weaker, would in that case have to possess a more expanded brain organ, in this case a more contracted one, or also precisely the reverse.
— Likewise whether its formation enlarged or diminished the organ, whether it made the same clumsier and thicker or finer.

By the fact that it remains indeterminate how the cause is constituted, it is likewise left indeterminate how the influence on the skull occurs, whether it is an expanding or a narrowing and a letting-collapse.
If this influence is perhaps more nobly determined as an excitation, then it is indeterminate whether it happens in the manner of a blistering plaster, swelling up, or of vinegar, shrinking.
— For all such views plausible grounds can be adduced, for the organic relation, which intervenes just as much, lets the one pass as well as the other and is indifferent to all this understanding.
zh: 但就自我意识的器官在其中会对那对立的一面成为起作用的原因的那种规定而言，人们可以以各种各样的方式来回谈论；因为这里谈的是一个原因的性状，这个原因是按其漠不相关的定在、按其形态和大小被考察的，而这个原因的内在东西和自为存在恰恰应当是那种丝毫不涉及直接定在的东西。
头颅的有机的自我形成首先对机械的作用是漠不相关的，而这两种关系的关系，既然前者是自身对自身的关联，就恰恰是这种无规定性和无界限性本身。

其次，即使脑把精神的那些差别作为存在着的差别接受到自身之中，并且是一个由占据不同空间的内部器官构成的多的东西，——这与自然相矛盾，因为自然给予概念的各个环节一种自己的定在，因而把有机生命的流动的单纯性完全放到一边，而把它的分节和划分同样在其差别中放到另一边，以至于它们，像它们在这里应当被把握的那样，显现为特殊的解剖学的东西——，那么也会是不确定的：一个精神环节，按照它原本是较强还是较弱，究竟在那种情况下必须拥有一个更扩张的脑器官、在这种情况下拥有一个更收缩的脑器官，还是恰好相反。
——同样也说不准：它的形成是使器官变大还是变小，是使同一个器官更粗笨、更厚，还是更精细。
由于原因是怎样的这一点始终不确定，对头颅的作用如何发生也就同样被留作不确定的，无论它是一种扩张，还是一种收窄和塌陷。
如果这种作用被更高贵地规定为一种激发，那么它究竟是以斑蝥硬膏的方式使其胀起，还是以醋的方式使其收缩，就是不确定的。
——对于所有这类看法，都可以提出一些显得有道理的理由，因为那种同样也参与进来的有机关系，让这一种和那一种一样行得通，并且对所有这一套知性都漠不相关。

en: But the observing consciousness is not concerned with wanting to determine this relation.
For in any case it is not the brain that stands on the one side as animal part, but the same as the being of self-conscious individuality.

— As standing character and self-moving conscious doing, it is for itself and in itself; over against this being-for-and-in-itself stands its actuality and determinate being for another; the being-for-and-in-itself is the essence and subject that has on the brain a being which is subsumed under it and receives its value only through the indwelling meaning.

But the other side of self-conscious individuality, the side of its determinate being, is being as independent and subject, or as a thing, namely a bone; the actuality and determinate being of man is his skull bone.
— This is the relation and the understanding that the two sides of this relation have in the consciousness observing them.
zh: 但观察的意识所关心的并不是要去规定这种关系。
因为站在一面上的，反正并不是作为动物性部分的脑，而是它作为自我意识的个体性的存在。
——它作为持存的性格和自身运动着的意识活动，是自为的并且在自身之中；同这种自为和在自身之中相对立的，是它的现实性和为他的定在；这种自为和在自身之中是本质和主体，它在脑上拥有一种存在，这种存在被归摄在它之下，并且只有通过内寓的含义才获得自己的价值。
而自我意识的个体性的另一面，即它的定在那一面，则是作为独立者与主体、或作为一个物、即一块骨头的那种存在；人的现实性和定在就是他的头颅骨。
——这就是这一关系的两个方面在观察着它们的意识中所具有的关系和知性。

en: This [consciousness] is now concerned with the more determinate relation of these sides; the skull bone does indeed in general have the meaning of being the immediate actuality of spirit.

But the many-sidedness of spirit gives its determinate being an equally manifold ambiguity; what is to be gained is the determinacy of the meaning of the individual places into which this determinate being is divided, and it is to be seen how they have the pointing to it on them.
zh: 现在，它所关心的则是这些方面之间更确定的关系；头颅骨在一般情况下的确具有这样的含义：它是精神的直接现实性。
但精神的多方面性使它的定在也具有一种同样的多义性；要争取到的是这种定在被划分成的各个个别位置在含义上的规定性，并且要看看它们在自己身上如何拥有那种对它的指示。

en: The skull bone is no organ of activity, nor yet a speaking movement; one neither steals, murders etc. with the skull bone, nor does it in the least pull a face for such deeds, so that it would become a speaking gesture.
— Nor does this existent have the value of a sign either.

Facial expression and gesture, tone, also a column, a post driven into a barren island, announce themselves at once as meaning that something else is still meant by them than what they immediately merely are.
They give themselves out at once as signs, in that they have on them a determinacy which points to something else by the fact that it does not belong to them as their own.

One can indeed, at a skull, as Hamlet at Yorick's2, let many things occur to one, but the skull bone for itself is so indifferent, unprejudiced a thing that on it immediately nothing else is to be seen and meant than only itself; it indeed reminds one of the brain and its determinacy, of skulls of another formation, but not of a conscious movement, since it has neither facial expression and gesture nor anything imprinted on it that would announce itself [as] coming from a conscious doing; for it is that actuality which was to present on individuality such an other side, which would no longer be being reflected into itself, but purely immediate being.
zh: 头颅骨不是活动的器官，也不是一种言说着的运动；人们既不用头颅骨去偷窃、杀人等等，它也丝毫不为这类行为做出表情，以至于它竟会成为言说着的姿势。
——这个存在者也同样不具有一个符号的价值。
表情和姿势、声音，还有一根柱子、一根钉在一座荒岛上的木桩，都立刻表明自己：借它们所意谓的还有某种别的东西，而不只是它们直接所是的东西。
它们立刻就把自己表明为符号，因为它们在自身那里具有一种规定性，这种规定性之所以指向某种别的东西，是因为它并不专属于它们。

人们固然也可以面对一个头颅，像哈姆雷特面对约里克的骷髅2那样，生出各种各样的念头，但头颅骨本身却是一个如此漠不相关、毫无成见的物，以至于在它身上直接既看不到、也意谓不出别的什么，而只有它自己；它固然使人想起脑及其规定性，想起构造不同的头颅，但不会使人想起一种意识活动，因为它既没有表情和姿势，也没有在自己身上压印着什么会表明自己是从一种意识活动而来的东西；因为它是那种现实性，这种现实性本应在个体性身上展示出这样一个另外的方面，这个方面不再是在自身中反思着自己的存在，而会是纯粹直接的存在。

en: Since, furthermore, it does not itself feel either, a more determinate meaning might still seem able to arise for it in this way: that determinate sensations would let one recognize, through the neighborhood, what is meant with it; and since a conscious mode of the spirit has its feeling at a determinate place of the same, this place would in its shape intimate that mode and its particularity.

Just as, for example, some complain that in strenuous thinking, or even in thinking in general, they feel a painful tension somewhere in the head, so too stealing, murdering, poetizing etc. could each be accompanied by a sensation of its own, which besides would still have to have its particular place.

This place of the brain, which in this way would be more moved and set in activity, would probably also form the neighboring place of the bone more; or, out of sympathy or consensus, the latter too would not be idle, but would enlarge or diminish itself or, in whatever way it be, form itself,

– What, however, makes this hypothesis improbable is this: that feeling in general is something indeterminate, and that feeling in the head as the center would be the universal fellow-feeling of all suffering, so that with the thief-murderer-poet-head-tickle or pain others would mix, and would be as little distinguishable from one another and from those that one can call merely bodily, as from the symptom of headache — if we restrict its meaning merely to the bodily — the illness can be determined.
zh: 此外，既然它自己也不感觉，那么对它来说似乎还可能这样得出一种更确定的意义：某些特定的感受会通过邻近关系让人认识到，它身上所指的是什么；而由于精神的某个有意识的方式在颅骨的某个特定位置上拥有自己的感受，这个位置就会以它的形态暗示那种方式及其特殊性。
例如，就像有些人在费力的思考时、或者甚至在一般地思考时，就抱怨在头脑里某处感到一种痛苦的紧张，偷窃、杀人、作诗等等也可以各自伴随着一种特有的感受，而这种感受此外还必须拥有它特殊的位置。
大脑的这个位置，以这种方式会更多地被运动和活动起来，它大概也会更多地养成骨骼的邻近位置；或者，后者出于同感或一致也不会懒惰，而是会变大或变小，或者无论以什么方式，把自己形成起来，
——不过，使这个假说变得不大可能的是：感受一般地是某种不确定的东西，而头脑里作为中心的感受会是这一切痛苦之普遍的共同感受，以致在偷儿—凶手—诗人—脑袋的痒或痛里会混进别的感受，而这些感受彼此之间、以及它们与那些只能叫作身体性的感受之间，会如此难以区分，就像从头痛的症状出发——如果我们把它的意义仅仅限制在身体性的东西上——无法确定疾病一样。

en: In fact, from whichever side the matter be considered, every necessary reciprocal relation, as well as its intimation speaking through itself, falls away.

If the relation is after all to take place, there remains, and necessarily so, a concept-less free pre-established harmony of the corresponding determination of both sides; for the one is supposed to be spirit-less actuality, a mere thing.
– Thus there stand on the one side a multitude of resting skull-places, on the other a multitude of spiritual properties, whose multiplicity and determination will depend on the state of psychology.

The more wretched the representation of the spirit is, the more the matter is facilitated from this side; for partly the properties become the fewer, partly the more separated off, firm and bony, and thereby all the more similar to and comparable with bone-determinations.

But although much is facilitated by the wretchedness of the representation of the spirit, there nevertheless always remains a very great multitude on both sides; there remains, for observation, the complete contingency of their relation.

If, of the children of Israel from the sand by the sea, to which they are supposed to correspond, each were to take for itself the little grain of which it is the sign, then this indifference and arbitrariness, which allotted to each its own, is just as strong as that which assigns to each soul-faculty, passion, and — what would here likewise have to be considered — the shadings of characters, of which the finer psychology and knowledge of human nature is accustomed to speak, their skull-places and bone-forms.

– The murderer's skull has this — not an organ, nor yet a sign, but this bump; but this murderer has besides a multitude of other properties as well as other bumps, and along with the bumps also depressions; one has a choice among bumps and depressions; and again his murderous sense can be related to whichever bump or depression it be, and in turn these can be related to whichever property it be; for neither is the murderer only this abstraction of a murderer, nor has he only one elevation and one depression.
The observations that are instituted about this must therefore sound just as good as the shopkeeper's and the housewife's rain at the fair and at the washing.
Shopkeeper and housewife could also make the observation that it always rains when this neighbor passes by or when roast pork is eaten.
As the rain is indifferent toward these circumstances, so indifferent is, for observation, this determinacy of the spirit toward this determinate being of the skull.

For of the two objects of this observing, the one is a dry being-for-itself, a bony property of the spirit, while the other is a dry being-in-itself, a thing as bony as both are, and it is completely indifferent toward everything else; it is just as indifferent to the high bump whether a murderer is in its neighborhood, as it is to the murderer whether flatness is in his vicinity.
zh: 事实上，无论从哪一面来看这件事，一切必然的相互关系以及这种关系那种自身言说着的暗示，都消失了。
如果这种关系毕竟还是要发生，那么剩下的、并且必然剩下的，就是双方相应规定之间一种无概念的、自由的预定和谐；因为其中一方应当是无精神的现实性，是单纯的物。
——于是，恰恰在一边立着一大堆静止的颅骨位置，在另一边立着一大堆精神属性，后者的多样性和规定将取决于心理学所处的状态。
关于精神的表象越是可怜，从这一面看事情就越是被弄得容易；因为一方面属性会变得越来越少，另一方面会变得越来越分离、越来越坚实、越来越骨质化，由此与骨骼规定越来越相似、越来越可比。
但是，尽管由于关于精神的表象之可怜，许多东西被弄得容易了，双方却始终还剩下很大的一堆；对观察来说，剩下的就是它们之关系的完全偶然性。
如果以色列的子孙要从海边的沙子里——他们应当与这沙子相对应——各自取出以自己为标记的那一粒沙，那么这种给每一个分派其应有之物的漠不关心和任意，就与那种漠不关心和任意一样强，后者给每一种灵魂能力、激情，以及——这里同样必须加以考察的——性格的种种色调（更精细的心理学和人情知识惯于谈论这些色调）分派其颅骨位置和骨骼形式。
——凶手的颅骨有这个——不是器官，也不是标记，而是这个隆起；但这个凶手还有许多别的属性以及别的隆起，并且与隆起一起还有凹陷；人们在隆起和凹陷之间有得选；而他的杀人意念又可以——无论涉及哪一个隆起或凹陷——与之相关联，反过来，这些隆起或凹陷又可以——无论涉及哪一种属性——与之相关联；因为凶手既不只是凶手这个抽象物，也不只有一处隆起和一处凹陷。
因此，在这方面所作的那些观察，听起来也必定和小贩与主妇在集市上、在洗衣时所说的那场雨一样好。
小贩和主妇也能作这样的观察：每当这个邻居走过，或者每当吃烤猪肉时，天总是下雨。
正如雨对这些情况漠不关心，对观察来说，精神的这种规定性对颅骨的这种特定存在也同样漠不关心。
因为在这种观察的两个对象中，一个是干巴巴的自为存在，是精神的一种骨质属性，正如另一个是干巴巴的自在存在，是一个与两者一样骨质的物，它完全漠不关心一切别的东西；高隆起对是否有一个凶手在它近旁同样无所谓，正如凶手对是否有一处平坦在他近旁无所谓。

en: To be sure, the possibility that a bump at some place be connected with some property, passion etc. remains insuperably left over.
One can represent the murderer with a high bump here at this skull-place, the thief with one there.

From this side the science of the skull is still capable of great expansion; for to begin with it seems to restrict itself only to the connection of a bump with a property in the same individual, so that this individual possesses both.

But even natural science of the skull — for there must be such a one as well as a natural physiognomy — goes beyond this limit; it judges not only that a clever human being has a fist-thick bump sitting behind the ears, but also represents that the unfaithful wife has bumps on her forehead not herself but the other marital individual.

– Likewise one can represent to oneself the one who lives under the same roof with the murderer, or also his neighbor and, further out, his fellow citizens etc., as having high bumps at some skull-place, just as well as the flying cow that was first caressed by the crab that rode on the donkey and afterward etc.

– If, however, the possibility is taken not in the sense of the possibility of representing, but of inner possibility or of the concept, then the object is such an actuality as is and is supposed to be a pure thing and without any such meaning, and can therefore have it only in representation.
zh: 当然，某种属性、激情等等与某处的一个隆起相联结，这种可能性不可克服地留存着。
人们可以设想凶手在这里这个颅骨位置上有一个高隆起，小偷在那边有一个。
从这一面看，颅骨科学还能有很大的扩展；因为起初它似乎只把自己限制在一个隆起与同一个体身上某种属性的联结，以致这个个体兼有两者。
但自然的颅骨科学——因为既有一种自然的面相学，也就必定同样有一种自然的颅骨科学——已经超出了这个界限；它不仅判断一个狡猾的人耳朵后面坐着一个拳头大的隆起，而且还设想：不忠的妻子额头上长隆起的不是她自己，而是另一个婚姻中的个体。
——同样，人们也可以设想那个与凶手同住在一个屋顶下的人，或者他的邻居，再往外还有他的同胞等等，在某个颅骨位置上长着高隆起，就像设想那头飞牛一样：它先是被那只骑在驴上的螃蟹抚爱，后来又等等。
——但如果这种可能性不是就表象的可能性、而是就内在的可能性或概念而言来理解，那么对象就是这样一种现实性：它是、并且应当是纯粹的物，没有诸如此类的意义，因而只能在表象中拥有这种意义。

en: If, however, despite the indifference of both sides, the observer nevertheless proceeds to the work of determining relations — kept fresh partly by the universal ground of reason that the outer is the expression of the inner, partly supporting himself with the analogy of the skulls of animals, which may indeed have a simpler character than human beings, but of which it becomes at the same time all the harder to say which one they have, since it cannot be so easy for the representation of every human being to form itself properly into the nature of an animal — then the observer finds, in the assurance of the laws that he wants to have discovered, an excellent help in a distinction that must here necessarily also occur to us.
– The being of the spirit can at least not be taken as something absolutely fixed and immovable.

The human being is free; it is conceded that the original being is only predispositions, over which he has much power or which need favorable circumstances in order to be developed; i.e. an original being of the spirit is just as much to be expressed as such a one that does not exist as being.

If, then, observations contradicted that which occurs to someone to assure as law — be it fine weather at the fair or at the washing — then shopkeeper and housewife could say that it really ought to rain and that the predisposition to it is nevertheless present; likewise the skull-observing, — that this individual really ought to be as the skull declares according to the law, and has an original predisposition which, however, has not been developed; this quality is not present, but it ought to be present.

– The law and the ought ground themselves on the observation of the actual rain and of the actual sense in this determinacy of the skull; but if the actuality is not present, then the empty possibility counts for just as much.

– This possibility, i.e. the non-actuality of the posited law and thereby observations contradicting it, must come in precisely through this: that the freedom of the individual and the developing circumstances are indifferent toward being in general, both toward it as original inner being and as outer bony being, and that the individual can also be something other than it is inwardly originally and still more than a bone is.
zh: 可是，尽管双方漠不关心，如果观察者还是着手去规定种种关系——他一方面被那条普遍的理性根据保持新鲜：外在的东西是内在东西的表达，另一方面又借助动物颅骨的类比来支持自己（动物颅骨虽然也许具有比人更简单的性格，但同时要说清它们具有哪一种性格却同样更难，因为并不是每个人的表象都能那么容易地把自己真正培养到一种动物的本性里去）——，那么观察者在确信他自以为发现了的那些规律时，就会在一个差别那里找到极好的帮助，而这个差别在这里也必然会使我们想到。
——精神的存在至少不能被当作某种绝对固定不动、不可移动的东西。
人是自由的；人们承认，那原初的存在只是些禀赋，人对它们有很大支配力，或者它们需要有利的情况才能被发展出来；也就是说，精神的一种原初存在同样要表述为这样一种东西：它并不作为存在而存在。
因此，如果观察与某人想起要当作规律来担保的东西相矛盾——不管是集市上或洗衣时的好天气——，那么小贩和主妇就可以说：其实本该下雨，而对此的禀赋毕竟现成存在；颅骨观察也同样可以这样说：这个个体其实本该像颅骨按规律所说的那样，并且具有一种原初的禀赋，只是这种禀赋没有被培养出来；这种品质并不现成存在，但它本该现成存在。
——规律和应当建立在对于现实的雨、以及对于颅骨的这种规定性身上现实的意义的观察之上；但如果现实性并不现成存在，那么空洞的可能性就同样算数。
——这种可能性，即所建立的规律之非现实性以及由此与它相矛盾的观察，必然恰恰由此进来：个体的自由和那些起发展作用的情况对一般存在漠不关心，既对作为原初内在东西的存在漠不关心，也对作为外在骨质东西的存在漠不关心，并且个体也可以成为某种别的东西，既不同于它内在地原初所是的东西，更不同于一块骨头。

en: We thus obtain the possibility that this bump or depression of the skull designates both something actual and also merely a disposition, and indeed one that is indeterminate with respect to anything whatever, that it designates something non-actual; we see a bad excuse fare as always, namely that it must itself be used against that very thing which it is supposed to help up.

We see meaning brought by the nature of the matter to itself say, though thoughtlessly, the opposite of what it holds fast; – to say that through this bone something or other is intimated, but just as well not.
zh: 于是我们就得到这样一种可能：颅骨的这种隆起或凹陷既标示某种现实的东西，又只标示一种禀赋，而且是对随便什么东西都不确定的禀赋，也就是说，它标示某种非现实的东西；我们看到，一个糟糕的借口总是同样的下场：它不得不被用来对付它本该扶助的那个东西。
我们看到，意谓被事情的本性弄到竟然自己说出它所坚持的那个东西的反面，不过是无思想地说出；——说出：通过这块骨头暗示出某种东西，但同样地也并非如此。

en: What hovers before the opinion itself in this excuse is the true thought, which precisely annihilates it, that being as such is not at all the truth of spirit.
Just as the disposition is already an original being that has no share in the activity of spirit, so the bone in its turn is likewise such a one.

The existent without spiritual activity is a thing for consciousness, and so little is it its essence that it is rather the opposite of the same, and consciousness is alone actual only through the negation and annihilation of such a being.

– From this side it is to be regarded as a complete denial of reason to pass off a bone as the actual determinate being of consciousness; and it is passed off as such in that it is considered as the outer of spirit, for the outer is precisely existing actuality.
It helps nothing to say that from this outer one only infers the inner, which is something else; that the outer is not the inner itself but only its expression.
For in the relation of the two to each other, the determination of the self-thinking and thought falls precisely on the side of the inner, but that of existing actuality on the side of the outer.
– If, then, it is said to a human being: you (your inner) are this, because your bone is so constituted, it means nothing other than: I regard a bone as your actuality.

The rejoinder to such a judgment by a box on the ear, mentioned in connection with physiognomy, first brings the soft parts out of their look and position and only proves that these are no true in-itself, not the actuality of spirit; here the rejoinder would really have to go so far as to smash in the skull of one who judges thus, in order to prove, just as palpably as his wisdom is, that a bone is nothing in itself for the human being, much less his true actuality.
zh: 意见自己在这个借口里所浮现出来的，恰恰是那个真实的、恰好把它消灭掉的思想：存在本身根本不是精神的真理。
正如禀赋已经是一种原初的存在，它在精神的活动中没有任何份，骨头这边同样也是这样一种东西。
没有精神活动的存在者，对意识来说是一个物，它远不是意识的本质，反倒恰恰是意识的反面，而意识只有通过对这样一种存在的否定和消灭才是现实的。
——从这一方面看，把一块骨头冒充为意识的现实定在，要算作对理性的完全否认；而它之所以被这样冒充，是因为它被看作精神的外在，因为外在恰恰就是存在着的现实性。
说从这个外在只能推论出内在，而内在是某种别的东西，说外在并不是内在本身、而只是它的表达，这都无济于事。
因为在这两者彼此的关系中，恰恰是思维着自身并被思维的规定落在内在这一边，而存在着的现实性的规定则落在外在这一边。
——所以，如果对一个人说：你（你的内在）是这样，因为你的骨头生得如此，那么这无非是说：我把一块骨头看作你的现实性。
面相学那里提到过用一记耳光来回应这样一种判断，这首先把柔软的部分打出它们原来的样子和位置，只证明这些部分不是真正的自在，不是精神的现实性；在这里，这种回应其实还必须走得更远，把这样作判断的人的颅骨敲碎，以便恰恰像他的智慧那样可触地证明：一块骨头对人来说并不是什么自在的东西，更不是他真正的现实性。

en: The crude instinct of self-conscious reason will reject a skull-science without looking at it – this other observing instinct of the same, which has ripened to a presentiment of cognition and has grasped it in the spirit-less way that the outer is the expression of the inner.
But the worse the thought is, the less it sometimes strikes one wherein its badness precisely lies, and the harder it is to take it apart.
For the thought counts as so much the worse, the purer and emptier the abstraction is that counts as essence for it.
